doc.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Festival etiquette and unfamiliar tunes
summary: Gordon describes playing unrehearsed festival sets, occasionally not knowing bebop melodies, and clarinet taking the first chorus in California.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I’ll be interested to hear you play tonight. Have you ever been in a situation in these festivals where you don’t know a tune?

Oh on some of them I have. I’ve been at really slick festivals where they are playing some bebop and I’m not too familiar with that type of music and I’ve tried to play it, and I know the chord progressions but maybe the melody I didn’t know. But I’ve been in situations like that yes.
Now what will happen this evening as far as, I know you guys don’t rehearse. Will there be a talk through if you’re playing in an ensemble?

No there’ll just, maybe just in the beginning maybe Marty might say something that we’re going to play this in this certain key and I’ve got the first chorus or you’ve got the second chorus. There’s that. But usually it’s just a free for all, everybody just goes around and everybody plays what they want to play.
And there’s a jazz etiquette I suppose, to be learned.
I don’t know if they teach that in schools.
I don’t know about California, but when I was in New York the clarinet always used to take the second or third chorus, but in California the clarinet seems to take the first
chorus all the time and I got kind of instilled in that, so I usually wind up taking the first chorus.
